newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel shares stronger as trains roll.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel shares stronger as trains roll.

text.p: Shares in Anglo-French Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel strengthened 1.5p to 82p by 0945 GMT after news that 90 percent of the Eurostar passenger service, which had been derailed by a fire, had restarted.

Eurotunnel said on Tuesday it also planned to start its Le Shuttle passenger vehicle services from December 10, although some analysts voiced uncertainty that the debt-laden company would be able to keep to that timetable.
"It now remains to be seen if they can prise people away from the ferries," said Peter Bergius, analyst at brokers ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.

Berguis said he had expected Eurostar inter-city express trains to resume trips between London, Paris and Brussels this week and added it would be good news if Le Shuttle services began next week, as promised.
About six trains per hour are able to use the tunnel compared to the usual nine.
The tunnel had been closed to all passenger traffic since November 18, when a fire on a truck destroyed a freight shuttle train and severely damaged a section on the tunnel, injuring 34 people.
